V1.name: Non-visual access to text and interface content
V1.definition: Use screen readers or equivalent non-visual representations to read, navigate, and act on digital text, controls, documents, and web content.

V2.name: Magnification and text enlargement
V2.definition: Enlarge text, controls, or the screen through zoom, text sizing, or magnification so that content is perceivable and usable.

V3.name: Contrast and display adaptation
V3.definition: Adjust contrast, foreground/background presentation, inversion, or display palette to improve visual readability.

V4.name: Color differentiation support
V4.definition: Use color filters or non-color cues when color differences are difficult or impossible to distinguish.

V5.name: Access to non-text visual information
V5.definition: Obtain equivalent information from images, maps, charts, infographics, scanned documents, labels, and other visual-only or poorly described content.

H1.name: Text/non-auditory access to speech and audio
H1.definition: Access spoken and relevant non-speech audio information through captions, transcripts, or another non-auditory representation.

H2.name: Caption presentation and language adaptation
H2.definition: Configure caption language and visual presentation so caption text is readable and appropriate for the media being consumed.

H3.name: Visual/persistent alternatives to auditory alerts
H3.definition: Receive alerts visually rather than by sound alone and keep visual notifications available long enough to notice and read.

H4.name: Audio-channel adaptation
H4.definition: Adapt audio channels so that information remains available through the user's usable listening channel.

M1.name: Alternative text entry
M1.definition: Enter text through an on-screen keyboard, speech, or another alternative input when conventional physical-keyboard entry is difficult.

M2.name: Keyboard interaction adaptation
M2.definition: Adapt keyboard timing, sensitivity, repetition, or multi-key input so keyboard interaction does not require simultaneous presses or precise key timing.

M3.name: Alternative/adapted pointer control
M3.definition: Use keyboard, speech, an alternative pointing method, delegated activation, or adapted pointer settings when conventional mouse use is difficult.

M4.name: Reduced fine-motor, precision, dragging, repetition, and timing demand
M4.definition: Avoid or delegate interactions requiring sustained press-hold-drag movements, repeated precise target acquisition, small-target selection, fine motor control, or tightly timed action.

C1.name: Attention and distraction reduction
C1.definition: Reduce distraction, competing stimuli, and visual or cognitive clutter so that attention can be directed and sustained.

C2.name: Readability and comprehension simplification
C2.definition: Reduce reading and language-processing demand through clearer presentation, simpler language, or better-structured content.

C3.name: Memory externalization and persistent information support
C3.definition: Reduce reliance on working memory or short-term retention by creating or using notes, checklists, persistent cues, and other durable external representations.

C4.name: Time and prospective-memory support
C4.definition: Use reminders, calendars, timers, notification persistence, and other time-based cues to manage appointments, deadlines, intervals, and future actions.
